subject: ipc
source: International Primary Curriculum (IPC), Milepost 3 thematic units (ages 9–12), Fieldwork Education; science content aligned to the English National Curriculum (Years 5–6)

weeks.topic: Mission to Mars — Entry point: our Solar System
objectives: Name and order the planets of the Solar System
Describe the Sun as a star at the centre
Share what we already know about space (knowledge harvest)

weeks.topic: Mission to Mars — Science: Earth, Moon and the movement of planets
objectives: Describe the movement of the Earth and planets relative to the Sun
Describe the movement of the Moon relative to the Earth
Use Earth's rotation to explain day and night

weeks.topic: Mission to Mars — Science: gravity, air resistance and forces
objectives: Explain that unsupported objects fall because of gravity
Investigate air resistance with parachutes
Compare gravity on Earth and on Mars

weeks.topic: Mission to Mars — Technology: designing a Mars rover
objectives: Research the conditions on Mars
Design and build a model rover using gears or levers
Evaluate the design against criteria

weeks.topic: Mission to Mars — History: the Space Race and Moon landing
objectives: Place key space events on a timeline
Explain why the 1969 Moon landing was significant
Use sources to find out about astronauts

weeks.topic: Mission to Mars — International & exit point: space cooperation
objectives: Explore how countries cooperate on the International Space Station
Present a plan for a mission to Mars
Reflect on learning from the unit

weeks.topic: AD 900 — Entry point: the world in AD 900
objectives: Locate civilisations of AD 900 on a world map
Compare what different places were like at the same time
Ask questions to investigate

weeks.topic: AD 900 — History: the Vikings, raiders and traders
objectives: Describe Viking life, longships and trade routes
Explain why Vikings raided and settled
Use evidence from archaeology

weeks.topic: AD 900 — History: the Maya civilisation
objectives: Describe Maya cities, writing and number system
Explore Maya beliefs and achievements
Compare the Maya with the Vikings

weeks.topic: AD 900 — History: Baghdad and the House of Wisdom
objectives: Describe Baghdad as a centre of learning in AD 900
Identify scientific and mathematical achievements of the time
Explain how knowledge spread

weeks.topic: AD 900 — Exit point: comparing civilisations on a timeline
objectives: Compare the three civilisations on a shared timeline
Explain similarities and differences
Present findings as a museum display

weeks.topic: Active Planet — Entry point: the structure of the Earth
objectives: Describe the layers of the Earth: crust, mantle and core
Build a model of the Earth's structure
Share questions about natural hazards

weeks.topic: Active Planet — Geography: tectonic plates and earthquakes
objectives: Explain how tectonic plates move
Describe what happens during an earthquake
Locate major plate boundaries on a world map

weeks.topic: Active Planet — Geography: volcanoes
objectives: Describe the parts of a volcano
Explain why volcanoes erupt
Locate famous volcanoes such as the Ring of Fire

weeks.topic: Term 1 review: space, AD 900 and the active Earth
objectives: Revisit key ideas from Mission to Mars and AD 900
Revisit Earth's structure, earthquakes and volcanoes
Reflect on learning goals

weeks.topic: Active Planet — Science: rocks and the rock cycle
objectives: Compare igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks
Explain how rocks form and change
Group rocks by their properties

weeks.topic: Active Planet — International & exit point: living with hazards
objectives: Compare how people in different countries prepare for hazards
Design a hazard safety guide
Reflect on the unit

weeks.topic: Fit for Life — Entry point: what keeps us healthy?
objectives: Discuss the factors that keep our bodies healthy
Record a personal health diary
Set questions for the unit

weeks.topic: Fit for Life — Science: the heart and circulatory system
objectives: Identify the main parts of the circulatory system
Describe the functions of the heart, blood vessels and blood
Measure and record pulse rate

weeks.topic: Fit for Life — Science: nutrition and a balanced diet
objectives: Identify food groups and their nutrients
Explain the impact of diet on the body
Plan a balanced meal

weeks.topic: Fit for Life — Science/PE: exercise and fitness investigation
objectives: Investigate the effect of exercise on pulse rate
Record results in tables and graphs
Draw conclusions from data

weeks.topic: Fit for Life — Society & exit point: health campaigns
objectives: Compare health campaigns from different countries
Design a health campaign for the school
Present it to an audience

weeks.topic: Making New Materials — Entry point: properties of materials
objectives: Compare materials by hardness, transparency, conductivity and magnetism
Group materials by their properties
Explain why materials are chosen for a purpose

weeks.topic: Making New Materials — Science: dissolving and separating mixtures
objectives: Know that some materials dissolve to form a solution
Separate mixtures by filtering, sieving and evaporating
Plan a fair test

weeks.topic: Making New Materials — Science: reversible and irreversible changes
objectives: Identify reversible changes such as melting and dissolving
Explain that some changes create new materials
Investigate burning and rusting safely

weeks.topic: Making New Materials — Technology & exit point: inventing a product
objectives: Research inventors of new materials
Design a product using a new material
Evaluate and present the product

weeks.topic: Mid-year assessment: IPC learning goals
objectives: Show knowledge from the Term 1 and 2 units
Explain scientific ideas with vocabulary
Apply skills to new questions

weeks.topic: Going Global — Entry point: where do our things come from?
objectives: Investigate where everyday products are made
Map product origins on a world map
Ask questions about global trade

weeks.topic: Going Global — Geography: trade and globalisation
objectives: Explain what globalisation means
Describe how goods travel around the world
Identify benefits and problems of global trade

weeks.topic: Going Global — Society: fair trade and producers
objectives: Explain how fair trade helps producers
Compare the lives of producers in different countries
Debate the price of a product

weeks.topic: Going Global — Geography: transport and carbon footprint
objectives: Calculate how far goods travel
Explain what a carbon footprint is
Suggest ways to reduce our footprint

weeks.topic: Going Global — International & exit point: connected cultures
objectives: Explore how food, music and language spread between cultures
Celebrate cultures represented in our school
Present a global fair

weeks.topic: Being Human — Entry point: how do we grow and change?
objectives: Describe the changes as humans develop from birth to old age
Discuss changes during puberty sensitively
Gather questions about growing up

weeks.topic: Being Human — Science: life cycles of plants and animals
objectives: Compare the life cycles of mammals, amphibians, insects and birds
Describe reproduction in plants
Draw and label life cycle diagrams

weeks.topic: Being Human — Exit point: identity and values
objectives: Reflect on personal identity and values
Explore what makes us human
Present a personal identity project

weeks.topic: End-of-year assessment: IPC learning goals
objectives: Show knowledge from the Year 5 units
Explain scientific ideas using vocabulary
Apply skills to unfamiliar questions

weeks.topic: Year 5 IPC review and reflection
objectives: Reflect on the Year 5 units and personal learning goals
Share favourite learning moments
Set goals for Year 6
